title: Context files that remember for you

scenes.headline: Context files that remember for you
scenes.sub: Write it once. Every session starts smart.
lines: Lesson two. Context files.
Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.
This is the single biggest upgrade most people never make.

scenes.headline: Say it once. Reuse it forever.
lines: Every new session starts with a blank memory.
So you end up explaining your stack, your style, and your rules, again and again.
A context file fixes that. You write it once, and the agent reads it first, every time.

scenes.headline: It's just markdown.
lines: Here's a real one. It's just a markdown file in your project.
A line about the stack.
Things to always do, like running the tests.
And things to never do, like committing secrets.
scenes.code:
# Project rules

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, pnpm.

## Always
- Run `pnpm test` before saying done
- Small commits, clear messages

## Never
- Edit files in /dist
- Commit .env files

scenes.headline: Short beats complete.
lines: A few tips.
Keep it short. Under two hundred lines.
Write rules, not essays.
And every time the agent gets something wrong, add a line, so it never happens again.
